chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Ismail, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The divorce of the intoxicated one is not with anything.
ai.seo_question: Is a divorce valid if the husband is drunk?
ai.summary: This concise hadith from al-Kafi establishes that the divorce of an intoxicated person (sukran) is valid and effective, a ruling derived from the principle that intoxication does not equate to total loss of sanity (junun) which would nullify legal acts. In Shia jurisprudence, this distinction is crucial as it differentiates between temporary impairment due to alcohol and permanent mental incapacity, ensuring marital stability is not easily dissolved by voluntary intoxication. The brevity of the report underscores its status as a foundational legal precedent in the chapters of divorce.
